projects.title: Techcon GH LLC – Infrastructure Deployment
projects.description: Review the requirements for Techcon GH LLC, build the environment on your own system, and use each section as the technical specification for the project. This project provides exact requirements, but it does not provide implementation steps.

sections.title: Instructions
sections.summary: Use this page as the project specification while you build the environment independently on your own system.

blocks.title: How to Use This Project
items: Read the active section carefully before you configure the related part of the environment.
Build the environment on your own system using the exact requirements listed in each section.
Move between sections as needed while you design, configure, validate, and troubleshoot the environment.
Treat the requirement tables, group design, folder structure, and policy settings as the required target state for the project.
Use the Mark as Reviewed control when you are satisfied that a requirement area has been fully addressed in your build.

blocks.title: Project Design Standard
items: This is a project, not a guided lab.
The environment must be designed and implemented from the requirements only.
The site provides the exact technical specification, but it does not provide click-path instructions or step-by-step procedures.
You are expected to determine the appropriate order of work, tools, validation methods, and troubleshooting process.

sections.title: Scenario
sections.summary: This section provides the business context for the deployment and establishes the operating environment that the infrastructure must support.

blocks.title: Organization Overview
blocks.content: Techcon GH LLC is a growing technology consulting firm formalizing the internal infrastructure for its New York office. The company has outgrown a loosely managed standalone environment and now requires centralized authentication, organized directory administration, controlled IP address assignment, policy-based workstation management, secure file services, and resilient shared storage.

blocks.title: Business Requirement
blocks.content: The New York office will serve as the initial deployment site for a standardized Windows Server environment. The infrastructure must support daily business operations, departmental file access, user account administration, client integration, and shared services that can be maintained in a professional business environment.

blocks.title: Business Units
items: The environment must support the following departments: Sales, Marketing, Operations, Human Resources, and IT.
The IT department includes the following operational teams: NOC, SOC, and Datacenter.

The completed environment must provide centralized authentication, structured Active Directory administration, controlled file access, policy enforcement, and a domain-joined client experience aligned to the business requirements.

sections.title: Server Configuration Requirements
sections.summary: This section defines the server inventory, role allocation, addressing standards, and storage configuration for the New York office deployment.

rows.label: TC-DC1
rows.value: 172.16.1.10/24 — Active Directory Domain Services, DNS, DHCP, Storage Replica

rows.label: TC-DC2
rows.value: 172.16.1.11/24 — Active Directory Domain Services, DNS, File Services, FSRM, Storage Replica

rows.label: Naming
rows.value: Computer names must be configured before server roles are installed

rows.label: IP Assignment
rows.value: Both servers must use static IPv4 addresses

rows.label: DNS Placement
rows.value: Both servers must use internal DNS appropriate for a domain controller deployment

rows.label: TC-DC1 Data Volume
rows.value: One additional 80 GB data disk for Storage Replica participation

rows.label: TC-DC2 Data Volume
rows.value: One additional 80 GB data disk for departmental shares, home folders, redirected folders, quotas, file screening, and Storage Replica participation

blocks.title: Server Expectations
items: Both servers must be able to communicate with each other over the network.
Both servers must be able to resolve each other by hostname.
Both servers must participate in Active Directory replication.
The environment must support authentication and internal name resolution when both domain controllers are online.
Storage Replica must be configured between TC-DC1 and TC-DC2.

sections.title: Active Directory Requirements
sections.summary: This section defines the domain design, FSMO placement, organizational structure, users, groups, and computer object placement for the environment.

items.title: Domain and Domain Controller Requirements
items.summary: These requirements define the forest, domain, and directory service expectations.

items: Promote TC-DC1 as the first domain controller in the forest.
Promote TC-DC2 as an additional domain controller in the same domain.
Directory replication must be functional between both domain controllers.
DNS data must be replicated between both domain controllers.

items.title: FSMO Role Requirements
items.summary: Final FSMO placement must match the role allocation shown below.

items: All five FSMO roles must be identified after the domain is deployed.
RID Master and PDC Emulator must be transferred to TC-DC2.
The final environment must reflect the FSMO placement shown in the table above.

items.title: OU Structure
items.summary: Directory objects must be organized according to the OU hierarchy below.

blocks.content:
TechconGH
│
├── Sales-Dep
│   ├── Sales-Users
│   ├── Sales-Groups
│   └── Sales-PCs
│
├── Marketing-Dep
│   ├── Marketing-Users
│   ├── Marketing-Groups
│   └── Marketing-PCs
│
├── Operations-Dep
│   ├── Operations-Users
│   ├── Operations-Groups
│   └── Operations-PCs
│
├── HR-Dep
│   ├── HR-Users
│   ├── HR-Groups
│   └── HR-PCs
│
├── IT-Dep
│   ├── IT-Users
│   ├── IT-Groups
│   └── IT-PCs
│
└── IT-Admins

items: User accounts must be created in the appropriate departmental Users OU.
Group objects must be created in the corresponding departmental Groups OU.
Client computer accounts must be placed in the appropriate departmental PCs OU.
Administrative accounts used to manage the environment must be separated under IT-Admins.

items.title: User Accounts
items.summary: Use realistic generic user identities and populate directory attributes consistently.

items: User objects must be created in the appropriate departmental Users OU.
Display names, department values, and titles must be populated consistently.
The logon naming standard must remain consistent across the environment.

items.title: Security Groups
items.summary: Role groups must be nested into department groups so broad access can be granted to the department while restricted access can be assigned to specific functions.

rows.label: Marketing
rows.value: Marketing-Managers, Content-Specialists, Digital-Marketing-Specialists, Brand-Coordinators, Campaign-Analysts, Communications-Associates, SEO-Specialists, Marketing-Assistants

rows.label: Operations
rows.value: Operations-Managers, Project-Coordinators, Service-Desk-Analysts, Procurement-Officers, Logistics-Coordinators, Operations-Analysts, Inventory-Officers, Facilities-Coordinators, Support-Technicians, Administrative-Officers

rows.label: Human Resources
rows.value: HR-Managers, HR-Officers, Payroll-Coordinators, Talent-Acquisition-Specialists, Employee-Relations-Officers, HR-Assistants

items: Each user must belong to the role group that matches the user’s function.
Each role group must be nested into its corresponding department group.
Department groups must be used when access should span the full department.
Specific role groups must be used when access must be restricted to a narrower function, such as Payroll, NOC, SOC, Datacenter, or departmental managers.
Permissions must not be assigned directly to user accounts.

items.title: Computer Accounts
items.summary: Client computer objects must be named consistently and placed in the correct organizational units.

rows.label: TC-CL1
rows.value: Required Windows 10/11 client — place in HR-PCs

rows.label: TC-CL2
rows.value: Optional Windows 10/11 client — place in IT-PCs or Sales-PCs for extended validation

items: At least one domain-joined client is required.
Client computer accounts must be moved to the correct departmental PCs OU after joining the domain.

sections.title: Network Requirements
sections.summary: This section defines the addressing model, DNS design, DHCP configuration, exclusions, and reservation behavior for the office network.

blocks.title: DNS Requirements
items: DNS must be installed on both domain controllers.
DNS data must replicate between both domain controllers.
Both servers must resolve each other by hostname.
Domain-joined clients must resolve internal resources using internal DNS.

blocks.title: Addressing Behavior
items: Infrastructure systems must not obtain IP addresses from DHCP.
Server IP addresses must be statically assigned within the excluded infrastructure range.
The client system TC-CL1 must always receive the same IP address from DHCP.
That persistent client address must be implemented using a DHCP reservation rather than static addressing on the client.

sections.title: File and Storage Requirements
sections.summary: This section defines the storage layout, departmental folders, access model, quotas, file screening, home folders, and storage replication expectations.

items.title: Storage Layout
items.summary: Both domain controllers must participate in the storage design because Storage Replica is required on both servers.

rows.label: TC-DC2 Data Volume
rows.value: 80 GB — Primary departmental data volume, home folders, redirected folders, quotas, file screening, and Storage Replica partner volume

items: File services must be hosted from TC-DC2.
Storage Replica must be configured between TC-DC1 and TC-DC2.
The replicated dataset must include the shared departmental data and user storage structure.

items.title: Access Model
items.summary: Access must align to the department-group and role-group model defined in Active Directory.

items: Permissions must be assigned through groups rather than directly to user accounts.
Department groups must be used when access spans the full department.
Role groups must be used for narrower access to management, payroll, NOC, SOC, or Datacenter data.

items.title: Home Folders, Quotas, and File Screening
items.summary: User storage must be centrally managed and controlled through FSRM.

items: Each user must have a dedicated home folder named with the user’s logon name under D:\Shares\Home.
Home folders must be accessible only to the user and administrators.
Folder redirection and mapped storage requirements must align with the home folder design.

sections.title: GPO Requirements
sections.summary: This section defines the required Group Policy configuration for account security, auditing, user environment controls, drive mapping, folder redirection, and workstation security.

items.title: GPO Design Standards
items.summary: Policies must be linked intentionally and targeted according to OU scope and management intent.

items: GPOs must be clearly named and linked at appropriate levels.
Policies must not be linked at the domain root unless domain-level scope is required.
User-focused and computer-focused settings must be targeted according to the relevant OU structure.
The IT-Admins OU must not receive standard workstation restrictions or user environment controls.

items.title: Domain Security Policy
items.summary: Account policies must be configured at the domain level.

items.title: Audit Policy
items.summary: Advanced auditing must capture key security and administrative events.

items: Audit Logon/Logoff — Success and Failure
Audit Account Logon — Success and Failure
Audit Object Access — Success
Audit Policy Change — Success
Audit Account Management — Success

items.title: User Environment Controls
items.summary: Standard users must receive restrictions and desktop standardization through Group Policy.

items: Disable Control Panel
Disable PC Settings
Block Command Prompt
Block Registry Editor
Configure a standard company wallpaper
Prevent users from changing the wallpaper

items.title: Drive Mapping and Folder Redirection
items.summary: Mapped drives and redirected folders must align to the department and home folder design.

items.title: Workstation Security Controls
items.summary: Client security settings must reinforce standard workstation hardening requirements.

items: Disable removable storage access
Enforce screen lock after 10 minutes
Require password on resume

sections.title: Client Requirements
sections.summary: This section validates the environment from the endpoint perspective and confirms that the infrastructure behaves correctly for a domain user.

blocks.title: Domain Integration Requirements
items: Join TC-CL1 to the techcongh.local domain.
Move the client computer account into the appropriate departmental PCs OU after the domain join.
The client must obtain its address configuration through DHCP.
The client must receive the reserved address assigned through DHCP reservation.

blocks.title: User Validation
items: Log in with at least one HR user account.
Log in with at least one IT user account for extended validation.
Confirm that group-based access aligns with the user’s department and role.

blocks.title: Expected Behavior
items: The client must resolve domain resources through internal DNS.
Group Policies must apply correctly.
Mapped drives must appear according to the user’s department.
Folder redirection must place user data in the central home folder location.
Users must be able to access only the folders permitted by their group membership.

sections.title: Final Review
sections.summary: Use this section to confirm that the completed environment matches the project specification before you consider the deployment finished.

blocks.title: Completion Criteria
items: Both domain controllers are deployed and replicating successfully.
FSMO roles are placed according to the project requirements.
DNS resolves all internal resources correctly.
DHCP issues client leases correctly and preserves the required reservation for TC-CL1.
File shares, quotas, and file screening function according to the storage design.
Group-based permissions align to department groups and role groups.
Storage Replica is configured between TC-DC1 and TC-DC2.
Group Policies apply according to domain, OU, and user scope requirements.
The client experience reflects the intended department access, mapped drives, and redirected folders.
